added_models.model: In-vitro PD-L1 binding and PD-1 blockade assays (engineered PD-L1/PD-1 cell lines, CD4+ T-cell proliferation)

engagement.note: In-vitro assays showed sugemalimab binds human PD-L1 and blocks PD-1 binding; no human occupancy yet measured.
engagement.short: In vitro: binds and blocks PD-L1
engagement.quote: The results from the in vitro studies demonstrated that sugemalimab bound to human PD-L1, competitively blocked binding of PD-L1 to PD-1 and induced the proliferation of CD4+ T-lymphocytes and the production of IFN-γ and IL-2.
engagement.confidence_note: First-use year 2016 is a proxy from the nonclinical study codes (BCG-PS-16033, 0002-16010) in the EPAR; the in-vitro reports themselves are not public. model_kind ex_vivo because the enum has no in-vitro cell-line value.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the assays' first use, before the first-in-human study.

engagement.note: At the 1200 mg Q3W dose later used in the cHL phase 2, peripheral-leukocyte PD-L1 receptor occupancy was 100% at trough in every evaluable patient.
engagement.quote: At predose on Cycle 2 Day 1, all 5 evaluable patients showed 100% RO. At predose on Cycle 4 Day 1, a 100% RO was consistently observed in all 3 evaluable patients.
engagement.confidence_note: Regulator summary of study CS1001-101 phase 1b (NCT03312842, advanced solid tumours or lymphomas); n=5 and n=3 evaluable; the occupancy data are not peer-reviewed and it is not stated whether any cHL patients were among them. The cHL phase 2 (CS1001-202, NCT03505996) used the same 1200 mg Q3W dose.
engagement.judgement: Judgement call: the in-vitro assays predict that sugemalimab occupies PD-L1; flow-cytometric receptor occupancy on circulating leukocytes is a direct readout of that, and it was saturated. Paired by me (comparison_stated false): the EPAR reports the assays and the occupancy in the same section but does not set them against each other. Only sugemalimab has engagement data; tagitanlimab and benmelstobart have none public.
engagement.magnitude_basis: PD-L1 receptor occupancy on peripheral blood leukocytes at trough

added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (4- and 26-week GLP studies, NOAEL 200 mg/kg)

dose.note: Repeat-dose cynomolgus toxicology set a NOAEL of 200 mg/kg, a tolerability margin over the planned human exposure.
dose.quote: The proposed NOAEL of 200mg/kg in the 4w exposure study was acceptable (animal-to-human exposure margin of Cmax ~21x-26x and AUC ~21x-23x).
dose.confidence_note: First-use year 2016 is a proxy (GLP studies precede the first-in-human study registered 2017); the toxicology reports are not public, only the EPAR summary.
dose.judgement: Opening entry: the toxicology package that stated the tolerability margin before patients were dosed.

dose.note: Patients, including lymphoma, were dosed 3-40 mg/kg and 1200 mg Q3W with no DLT and no MTD; the cHL phase 2 then used 1200 mg Q3W.
dose.quote: The fixed dose of 1200 mg IV Q3W had acceptable safety and tolerability profiles. No DLT event occurred, and no MTD was obtained.
dose.confidence_note: Regulator summary of CS1001-101 phase 1a (advanced solid tumours or lymphomas); not peer-reviewed. The EPAR states the margin against clinical exposure (Cmax 577 µg/mL) and the phase 1a tolerability in separate sections. No cHL-specific tolerability data are published; CS1001-202 (cHL, n=80, 1200 mg Q3W) is only pooled in the EPAR safety set.
dose.reason: Margin held; no DLT at 1200 mg
dose.judgement: Judgement call: scored on the dose rule's margin half. The monkey NOAEL stated that exposures far above the clinical one were tolerated; patients were dosed to the chosen 1200 mg Q3W regimen without dose-limiting toxicity, so same with margin_stated true. The model stated no efficacy exposure target, so this says nothing about whether 1200 mg was enough in cHL. Paired by me from two EPAR sections (comparison_stated false). Sugemalimab only.

considered_not_added: 9p24.1 amplification as a patient-level selector (Chen 2022: five CS1001 non-responders all amplified): same system as the draft's chl-9p24-pdl1-genetics track, so not a missing model; a patient-level entry on that track is for the draft, as the checker noted

Humanised PD-1 mice bearing murine colon carcinoma (sugemalimab EPAR in-vivo efficacy, 3-30 mg/kg): an NSCLC-directed anti-tumour model the EMA called not robust; nobody compared it with cHL patient results and it is not the model the class entered cHL on

Cynomolgus toxicology ocular findings vs immune-mediated ocular reactions in patients (EPAR states both): the patient side is sugemalimab plus chemotherapy in NSCLC, outside this tile's cHL population

Sugemalimab population PK model (Wang 2025, Br J Clin Pharmacol; EPAR simulations for a 1500 mg dose above 115 kg): fitted to the patient data it describes, with no prospective dose prediction checked in cHL patients
Tagitanlimab (KL-A167) and benmelstobart (TQB2450): no public preclinical model, receptor-occupancy or dose-model data found; their cHL phase 2s (NCT03580564, NCT03800706) have no published results
Patient-derived cHL cells, PDX or organoids for anti-PD-L1: none found (cHL has very few tumour cells and no established PDX use for this class)
